newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria depo rates fall due to high lev supply.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria depo rates fall due to high lev supply.

text.p: Bulgarian interbank deposit rates fell on Tuesday as supply of lev funds topped demand, dealers said.
"Banks prefer to maintain high liquidity through forex sales instead of borrowing at the depo market and placing foreign currency as collateral," a dealer said.
Traders said that high lev fund supply led interbank lev deposit rates falling below dollar deposit rates which have traditionally been lower.
The overnight interbank dollar deposit rates are 6.0-6.5 percent annually while one-week rates are around seven percent.
Banks which have bought marks at lower levels in the past several weeks sold them to the central bank to profit from forex transaction costs, dealers said.
The central bank was buying marks at 995 levs and selling at 1,000 levs under the currency board mechanism launched on July 1 under which the lev is pegged to the mark at a rate of 1,000.

Overnight interbank depo rates fell to 4.5-5.0 percent annually from 5-6 percent on Monday, while deposits for up to seven days were borrowed at a simple annual interest of 6.0-6.5 percent, down from 7-8 percent.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 7.50 percent on Monday from 8.00 percent on Friday, a central bank official said.
The central bank cut its simple annual main interest rate to 9.76 percent from 10.12 percent, in force from Monday.
